title: Finite-horizon SMC error, CLTs, and degeneracy

items.title: Dobrushin contraction coefficient for a probability kernel
items.statement:
Let $(S,\Sigma)$ and $(E,\mathcal E)$ be measurable spaces with $S\ne\varnothing$, and let $K:S\rightsquigarrow E$ be a probability kernel as in [[def-measure-kernel-and-probability-kernel]]. Its **Dobrushin contraction coefficient** is
$$\delta(K):=\sup_{x,x'\in S}\lVert K(x,\cdot)-K(x',\cdot)\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}},$$
where $\lVert\cdot\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}$ is the event-supremum distance between probability laws in [[def-total-variation-distance-for-probability-laws]]. Thus $0\le\delta(K)\le1$. The coefficient measures the largest total-variation separation between two one-step output laws.

items.title: Uniform density ratios bound the Dobrushin coefficient
items.statement:
Let $K:S\rightsquigarrow E$ be a probability kernel on a nonempty measurable source space. Suppose a sigma-finite measure $\lambda$ on $E$ and probability densities $k_x$ satisfy $K(x,A)=\int_A k_x\,d\lambda$ for every $x\in S$ and measurable $A\subseteq E$. If $C\ge1$ and, for every $x,x'\in S$, $k_x(z)\le Ck_{x'}(z)$ for $\lambda$-almost every $z$, then the Dobrushin coefficient from [[def-dobrushin-coefficient-for-probability-kernels]] obeys
$$\delta(K)\le1-C^{-1}.$$

items.title: Finite-horizon SMC CLT classes and variance recursions
items.statement:
Fix a finite horizon $T$. At each $0\le t\le T$, let $\pi_t$ be a probability law on a measurable particle space $\Theta_t$. Let $\widetilde\pi_0$ be an initial proposal with $\pi_0\ll\widetilde\pi_0$, and fix $\upsilon_0=d\pi_0/d\widetilde\pi_0$. For $1\le t\le T$, let $k_t$ be a probability kernel from $\Theta_{t-1}$ to $\Theta_t$, and put
$$\widetilde\pi_t(A)=\int_{\Theta_{t-1}}k_t(x,A)\,\pi_{t-1}(dx).$$
Assume $\pi_t\ll\widetilde\pi_t$ and fix a nonnegative Radon–Nikodym version $\upsilon_t=d\pi_t/d\widetilde\pi_t$, so $\widetilde\pi_t(\upsilon_t)=1$. The BCS-41 sequential importance-resampling algorithm [[alg-sequential-importance-resampling]] is this scheme on path spaces when $k_t$ appends a proposal transition. Under the support and measurable versions of [[thm-feynman-kac-path-radon-nikodym-weight]], its normalized incremental weight is $\upsilon_t=(Z_{t-1}/Z_t)G_t r_t$ for $t\ge1$, and $\upsilon_0=G_0\rho_0/Z_0$ initially. The previous normalized target is already part of $\widetilde\pi_t$; one does not multiply by the full earlier path-weight product again.

For a measurable vector function $\phi:\Theta_t\to\mathbb R^d$, write $\mu(\phi)=\int\phi\,d\mu$ and
$$\operatorname{Cov}_{\mu}(\phi)=\int(\phi-\mu(\phi))(\phi-\mu(\phi))^\top\,d\mu,$$
when the second moment is finite. Also write $k_t\phi(x)=\int\phi(z)k_t(x,dz)$ and
$$\operatorname{Cov}_{k_t}(\phi)(x)=\int(\phi(z)-k_t\phi(x))(\phi(z)-k_t\phi(x))^\top k_t(x,dz).$$

The source recursive test classes are
$$\Phi_0^{(d)}=\{\phi:\widetilde\pi_0(\|\phi\|^2)<\infty\},$$
and, for $t\ge1$,
$$\Phi_t^{(d)}=\left\{\phi:\text{ for some }\delta>0,\ \widetilde\pi_t(\|\upsilon_t\phi\|^{2+\delta})<\infty\ \text{ and }\ x\mapsto k_t(\upsilon_t\phi)(x)\in\Phi_{t-1}^{(d)}\right\}.$$
Assume $1\in\Phi_t^{(1)}$ for every $t$. This is the source theorem's explicit normalizing-weight condition. For the recursive post-resampling CLTs proved on this page, use the stronger classes $\Psi_t^{(d)}$. At $t=0$, let $\Psi_0^{(d)}$ consist of the $\phi\in\Phi_0^{(d)}$ for which $\widetilde\pi_0(\|\upsilon_0(\phi-\pi_0(\phi))\|^2)<\infty$ and $\pi_0(\|\phi\|^2)<\infty$. The initial normalizing denominator needs only its finite first moment $\widetilde\pi_0(\upsilon_0)=1$. For $t\ge1$, let $\Psi_t^{(d)}$ consist of the $\phi\in\Phi_t^{(d)}$ for which $\pi_t(\|\phi\|^2)<\infty$ and $x\mapsto E_t(\phi-\pi_t(\phi))(x)\in\Psi_{t-1}^{(d)}$. Here $E_t h=k_t(\upsilon_t h)$ is the operator defined below. Only target second moments are required: fixed-tail truncation supplies the conditional selection Lindeberg condition without a target higher-moment assumption. The recursive target moments supply the offspring variance at every earlier selection used in the induction. The source $\Phi_t$ conditions alone need not imply them. The source condition $1\in\Phi_t$ and these recursive target moments are the stated hypotheses for the CLT induction; no higher initial normalizer moment is required.

Define the mutation covariance operators recursively. At time zero,
$$\widetilde V_0(\phi)=\operatorname{Cov}_{\widetilde\pi_0}(\phi).$$
For $t\ge1$,
$$\widetilde V_t(\phi)=\widehat V_{t-1}(k_t\phi)+\int\operatorname{Cov}_{k_t}(\phi)(x)\,\pi_{t-1}(dx).$$
The weighted-estimator covariance is
$$V_t(\phi)=\widetilde V_t\!\left(\upsilon_t(\phi-\pi_t(\phi))\right).$$
For a measurable vector function $h$ on $\Theta_t$, define the forward operator from $\Theta_{t-1}$ by
$$E_t h(x)=k_t(\upsilon_t h)(x)=\int\upsilon_t(z)h(z)\,k_t(x,dz).$$
For $k<t$, write $E_{k+1:t}=E_{k+1}\circ\cdots\circ E_t$; set $E_{t+1:t}$ to the identity operator.
For multinomial offspring resampling set
$$\widehat V_t^{\mathrm{multi}}(\phi)=V_t(\phi)+\operatorname{Cov}_{\pi_t}(\phi).$$
For residual offspring resampling, let $r(u)=u-\lfloor u\rfloor$. When $c_t=\widetilde\pi_t(r(\upsilon_t))>0$, define the formal source candidate
$$R_t^{\mathrm{cand}}(\phi)=\widetilde\pi_t\!\left(r(\upsilon_t)\phi\phi^\top\right)-\frac{\widetilde\pi_t(r(\upsilon_t)\phi)\,\widetilde\pi_t(r(\upsilon_t)\phi)^\top}{c_t}.$$
Set $R_t=R_t^{\mathrm{cand}}$ and $\widehat V_t^{\mathrm{res}}=V_t+R_t$ only when $\widetilde\pi_t(\upsilon_t\in\{1,2,\ldots\})=0$; then $c_t>0$ and the finite-sample floor discontinuities are avoided. If $\upsilon_t=1$ $\widetilde\pi_t$-almost everywhere, put $R_t=0$. Residual offspring are deterministic whenever all sampled weights equal one. In SIR this holds almost surely outside earlier zero-weight fallback events, whose probability tends to zero at a fixed horizon; the almost-everywhere condition alone does not prescribe weights on proposal-null states reached after a fallback. No residual covariance is assigned when $c_t=0$ but $\upsilon_t$ is not almost everywhere one: the finite-sample normalization can move positive integer weights across floor boundaries. The B-page counterexamples show why the general positive-integer-atom branch remains unassigned.

items.title: Uniform SMC backward-operator contraction controls oscillation
items.statement:
Let $E_s$ be the forward operators of [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]], and for bounded real $h$ put $\operatorname{osc}(h)=\sup h-\inf h$. Suppose there is one $\beta\in[0,1)$ such that
$$\operatorname{osc}(E_s h)\le\beta\operatorname{osc}(h)$$
for every $s$ and every bounded real $h$ with $\pi_s(h)=0$, with bounded measurable versions of $E_sh$. The stronger condition on every bounded $h$ is sufficient but is not necessary here. For bounded $\phi:\Theta_t\to\mathbb R$, put $\Delta\phi=\operatorname{osc}(\phi)$ and $\bar\phi=\phi-\pi_t(\phi)$. Then for every $0\le k\le t$,
$$\bigl\lVert E_{k+1:t}\bar\phi\bigr\rVert_\infty\le\beta^{t-k}\Delta\phi,$$
with $\beta^0=1$ and $E_{t+1:t}$ the identity. This condition concerns the actual SMC backward operators; it is not implied merely by mixing ratios of the proposal densities.

items.title: Finite-horizon SMC empirical laws converge for integrable tests
items.statement:
Use the finite-horizon target, proposal and mutation sequence of [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]], and run the SIR procedure of [[alg-sequential-importance-resampling]] with either multinomial or residual resampling at every selection. Let $X_t^{1:N}$ be the proposal particles after mutation and before correction, let $\eta_t^N=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N\delta_{X_t^i}$, and let
$$\omega_t^N=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^N\upsilon_t(X_t^i)\delta_{X_t^i}}{\sum_{i=1}^N\upsilon_t(X_t^i)}$$
when the denominator is positive, using the algorithm's uniform fallback otherwise. Let $\check\eta_t^N$ be the empirical probability measure of one offspring selection from $\omega_t^N$; for nonterminal times this is the population carried into the next mutation. For each fixed $t\le T$,
$$\eta_t^N(h)\xrightarrow{P}\widetilde\pi_t(h)\quad(h\in L^1(\widetilde\pi_t)),\qquad \omega_t^N(\phi)\xrightarrow{P}\pi_t(\phi),\qquad \check\eta_t^N(\phi)\xrightarrow{P}\pi_t(\phi)\quad(\phi\in L^1(\pi_t))$$
as $N\to\infty$. The terminal selection in $\check\eta_t^N$ is an auxiliary resampling output; it is not an extra finite-particle accuracy claim.

items.title: Multinomial SMC variance unrolls into local contributions
items.statement:
Use the operators and multinomial variance recursion of [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]] at every selection time. For $\phi\in\Psi_t^{(d)}$, put $\bar\phi=\phi-\pi_t(\phi)$. Then
$$V_t(\phi)=\sum_{k=0}^{t}\widetilde\pi_k\!\left[\upsilon_k^2\,E_{k+1:t}(\bar\phi)E_{k+1:t}(\bar\phi)^\top\right],$$
where the $k=t$ term uses $E_{t+1:t}\bar\phi=\bar\phi$. Each summand is a finite positive-semidefinite matrix under the stated class conditions.

items.title: Centered filtering Feynman–Kac operators contract terminal tests
items.statement:
Let $\mathsf X$ be a nonempty standard-Borel space with a sigma-finite reference measure $\lambda$, and let $\eta_0$ be a probability on it. For $s\ge1$, supply jointly measurable, strictly positive finite densities $g_s(z\mid x)$ of probability transition kernels relative to $\lambda$, and measurable likelihood factors $f_s$ with $0<a\le f_s(z)\le b<\infty$. These specified versions satisfy, for one $C\ge1$ and every $s,x,x',z$,
$$g_s(z\mid x)\le Cg_s(z\mid x').$$
Define $c_s=\eta_{s-1}(g_sf_s)$, $\eta_s(h)=\eta_{s-1}(g_s(f_sh))/c_s$, and $E_sh(x)=g_s(f_sh)(x)/c_s$. They are the operators of [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]] restricted to last-state tests in the corresponding filtering model. Put $\rho=1-C^{-2}$. For every bounded measurable real terminal test $\psi$ and $0\le k<t$,
$$\|E_{k+1:t}(\psi-\eta_t\psi)\|_\infty\le C\rho^{t-k}\operatorname{osc}(\psi).$$
For $k=t$ the identity image is bounded by $\operatorname{osc}(\psi)$; use $\rho^n=0$ for $n\ge1$ when $C=1$. This is a closed last-state-test assertion, not a contraction of arbitrary functions of the full stored path. Positivity, finiteness and the ratio bounds refer to the supplied pointwise density versions, not to unspecified unrelated null-set versions.

items.title: Conditional multinomial resampling central limit theorem
items.statement:
Fix a time $t$ in the finite-horizon SIR system of [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]]. Let $\omega_t^N$ be its corrected weighted empirical law and let $\check\eta_t^N$ be the empirical law after multinomial offspring resampling. Suppose $\pi_t(\phi^2)<\infty$, the empirical-law conclusions of [[lem-smc-finite-horizon-empirical-law]] hold, and
$$\sqrt N\{\omega_t^N(\phi)-\pi_t(\phi)\}\Rightarrow N(0,V)$$
for a finite $V\ge0$. Then
$$\sqrt N\{\check\eta_t^N(\phi)-\omega_t^N(\phi)\}\Rightarrow N(0,\operatorname{Var}_{\pi_t}(\phi)),$$
asymptotically independently of the weighted-estimator fluctuation, and
$$\sqrt N\{\check\eta_t^N(\phi)-\pi_t(\phi)\}\Rightarrow N\!\left(0,V+\operatorname{Var}_{\pi_t}(\phi)\right).$$

items.title: Conditional mutation and weighted correction CLT
items.statement:
Fix $t\ge1$. Suppose the selected empirical array at time $t-1$ has the CLT with covariance $\widehat V_{t-1}$ for $k_t\psi$. Let $\psi:\Theta_t\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $\widetilde\pi_t(|\psi|^{2+\delta})<\infty$ for some $\delta>0$ and $k_t\psi\in\Phi_{t-1}^{(1)}$. Then the proposal empirical mean after mutation satisfies
$$\sqrt N\left(\eta_t^N(\psi)-\widetilde\pi_t(\psi)\right)\Rightarrow N\!\left(0,\widehat V_{t-1}(k_t\psi)+\pi_{t-1}\!\left(\operatorname{Var}_{k_t}(\psi)\right)\right)=N(0,\widetilde V_t(\psi)).$$
For weighted correction, take $\psi=\upsilon_t(\phi-\pi_t(\phi))$ and explicitly require the preceding selected-population CLT for $k_t\psi=E_t(\phi-\pi_t(\phi))$. In particular, if $\phi\in\Psi_t^{(1)}$, $1\in\Phi_s^{(1)}$ for $0\le s\le t$, and this preceding selected CLT holds, the weighted corrected estimate satisfies
$$\sqrt N\left(\omega_t^N(\phi)-\pi_t(\phi)\right)\Rightarrow N(0,V_t(\phi)).$$
At $t=0$, a separate weighted-only conclusion holds whenever $\pi_0(|\phi|)<\infty$ and $Z=\upsilon_0(\phi-\pi_0\phi)\in L^2(\widetilde\pi_0)$: the weighted estimate has the ratio CLT with variance $V_0(\phi)=\widetilde\pi_0(Z^2)$. No target second moment, proposal second moment of $\phi$, or denominator second moment is required for this weighted-only conclusion. The stronger $\Psi_0$ assumptions imply it and support subsequent selected-population conclusions.

items.title: Conditional residual resampling central limit theorem away from integer weights
items.statement:
Fix a time $t$ in the finite-horizon SIR system of [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]]. Let $X_t^{1:N}$ have proposal empirical law $\eta_t^N$, corrected law $\omega_t^N$, and residual-resampled law $\check\eta_t^N$. Assume the proposal empirical law converges in probability for every integrable test as in [[lem-smc-finite-horizon-empirical-law]], the weighted estimate has a finite-variance CLT
$$\sqrt N\{\omega_t^N(\phi)-\pi_t(\phi)\}\Rightarrow N(0,V),$$
and $\pi_t(\phi^2)<\infty$. Write $u=\upsilon_t$ and assume either $u=1$ $\widetilde\pi_t$-almost everywhere, or
$$\widetilde\pi_t(u\in\{1,2,\ldots\})=0.$$
In the second case $c=\widetilde\pi_t(r(u))>0$. Then, with
$$R_t(\phi)=\widetilde\pi_t(r(u)\phi^2)-\frac{\widetilde\pi_t(r(u)\phi)^2}{c},$$
where $R_t(\phi)=0$ in the constant-weight case,
$$\sqrt N\{\check\eta_t^N(\phi)-\omega_t^N(\phi)\}\Rightarrow N(0,R_t(\phi)),$$
asymptotically independently of the weighted-estimator fluctuation, and
$$\sqrt N\{\check\eta_t^N(\phi)-\pi_t(\phi)\}\Rightarrow N(0,V+R_t(\phi)).$$

items.title: Time-uniform SMC asymptotic variance under uniform weight and operator bounds
items.statement:
Use multinomial offspring resampling and the covariance $V_t$ of [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]]. Suppose all normalized incremental weights satisfy $\upsilon_s\le B<\infty$ almost everywhere under their proposals, including $s=0$. For a chosen bounded real terminal test $\phi$ and every $0\le k\le t$, assume the bounded versions of its centered backward images satisfy
$$\|E_{k+1:t}(\phi-\pi_t\phi)\|_\infty\le A\rho^{t-k}\Delta\phi,$$
with fixed $A\ge1$ and $0\le\rho<1$, uniformly over the horizons considered; use $\rho^0=1$. Then
$$V_t(\phi)\le\frac{A^2B^2(\Delta\phi)^2}{1-\rho^2}.$$
The one-step centered oscillation condition of [[lem-smc-backward-operator-oscillation-bound]] gives the original specialization $A=1$, $\rho=\beta$ and bound $B^2(\Delta\phi)^2/(1-\beta^2)$.

There is a separate filtering-density sufficient branch. Use the strictly positive finite density versions, true-transition row-ratio bound $C\ge1$, likelihood bounds $0<a\le f_s\le b<\infty$ and normalized filtering operators in [[lem-smc-centered-filtering-feynman-kac-contraction]]. Additionally require strictly positive finite proposal densities $q_s(z\mid x)$ with $g_s(z\mid x)\le Dq_s(z\mid x)$ uniformly for a finite $D$, and an initial normalized weight $\upsilon_0\le B_{\rm init}<\infty$ under its proposal. Put $B=\max(B_{\rm init},Db/a)$ and $\rho=1-C^{-2}$. For bounded last-state tests $\phi(x_{0:t})=\psi(x_t)$, the bound holds with $A=C$:
$$V_t(\psi)\le\frac{B^2C^2(\operatorname{osc}\psi)^2}{1-(1-C^{-2})^2}.$$
This branch concerns the closed last-state test subspace and its backward images, not all path observables. Both bounds concern fixed-horizon CLT variances, uniform in the time index; neither is a finite-particle time-uniform error bound.

items.title: Fixed-horizon SMC central limit theorem with multinomial resampling
items.statement:
Fix a finite horizon $t$ and use the target/proposal flow and classes $\Phi_s^{(d)},\Psi_s^{(d)}$ of [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]], with $1\in\Phi_s^{(1)}$ for every $0\le s\le t$. Run the SIR procedure with multinomial resampling at each time. For $\phi\in\Psi_t^{(d)}$, let $\omega_t^N$ be the corrected weighted empirical law and $\check\eta_t^N$ the post-resampling empirical law. Then
$$\sqrt N\{\omega_t^N(\phi)-\pi_t(\phi)\}\Rightarrow\mathcal N_d(0,V_t(\phi)),\qquad
\sqrt N\{\check\eta_t^N(\phi)-\pi_t(\phi)\}\Rightarrow\mathcal N_d(0,\widehat V_t^{\rm multi}(\phi)),$$
where $\widehat V_t^{\rm multi}(\phi)=V_t(\phi)+\operatorname{Cov}_{\pi_t}(\phi)$. The horizon is fixed as $N\to\infty$; the theorem asserts no time-uniform finite-particle accuracy.

items.title: Fixed-horizon SMC central limit theorem with residual resampling away from integer weights
items.statement:
Fix a finite horizon $t$ and use the target/proposal flow and classes $\Phi_s^{(d)},\Psi_s^{(d)}$ of [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]], with $1\in\Phi_s^{(1)}$ for every $0\le s\le t$. Run SIR with residual resampling at each time. At every $0\le s\le t$, assume either $\upsilon_s=1$ $\widetilde\pi_s$-almost everywhere, or $\widetilde\pi_s(\upsilon_s\in\{1,2,\ldots\})=0$. For $\phi\in\Psi_t^{(d)}$, let $\omega_t^N$ be the corrected weighted empirical law and $\check\eta_t^N$ the post-resampling empirical law. Then
$$\sqrt N\{\omega_t^N(\phi)-\pi_t(\phi)\}\Rightarrow\mathcal N_d(0,V_t(\phi)),\qquad
\sqrt N\{\check\eta_t^N(\phi)-\pi_t(\phi)\}\Rightarrow\mathcal N_d(0,\widehat V_t^{\rm res}(\phi)),$$
where $\widehat V_s^{\rm res}=V_s+R_s$ is defined by [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]] in the stated branches. No conclusion is asserted for a nonconstant weight law with positive mass at a positive integer. The horizon is fixed as $N\to\infty$.

title: Finite-horizon SMC error, CLTs, and degeneracy — Examples

items.title: Ancestry collapse under repeated multinomial resampling
items.statement: Track $N=2$ particles with equal weights through $m\ge1$ repeated multinomial resampling steps and identity mutation. Use fresh independent randomness at each call: the $m$ pairs of child indices are mutually independent, each uniform on $\{1,2\}^2$. Each child records the original ancestor from which its state descends. The normalized particle weights remain $(1/2,1/2)$ at each step.

items.title: The source function class need not give finite SMC CLT variances
items.statement: The source class $\Phi_t$ in [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]], together with $1\in\Phi_t$, guarantees that every displayed finite-horizon weighted and post-resampling CLT covariance is finite, including $V_0$ for a separately weighted initial proposal.

items.title: Residual resampling is discontinuous at positive integer weights
items.statement: Under the recursive weighted-moment class and normalization hypotheses in [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]], the residual offspring covariance is always the displayed $R_t(\phi)$ computed from the limiting fractional parts $r(\upsilon_t)$, including when the importance-weight law has an atom at a positive integer.

items.title: Zero limiting remainder does not make finite residual offspring deterministic
items.statement: If $\widetilde\pi(r(\upsilon))=0$, then standard residual resampling has deterministic offspring counts for every finite particle sample, so its residual covariance may always be set to zero.

items.title: A dominant particle weight and the effective sample size
items.statement: Use proposal probabilities $q(A)=1/4$, $q(B)=3/4$ and target probabilities $\pi(A)=99/100$, $\pi(B)=1/100$. Compute the weight-based effective sample size for four proposal draws containing one $A$ and three $B$ values.

items.title: Proposal mixing ratios alone do not bound SMC asymptotic variance over time
items.statement: Uniform bounds on the true transition density ratios $g(x\mid x')/g(x\mid x'')$ and proposal density ratios $q_t(x\mid x')/q_t(x\mid x'')$, together with a likelihood bounded above and away from zero and a bounded test oscillation, suffice by themselves to keep the SIR asymptotic variance $V_t(\phi)$ bounded uniformly in time.

items.title: A bounded-weight mixing filter has bounded asymptotic variance
items.statement: Let $\mathsf X=\{0,1\}$, set the initial target and proposal to the uniform law, and use at every step the true transition and proposal kernel $K(x,\cdot)=(1/2,1/2)$, with constant likelihood one. Thus all incremental weights equal one. For $\phi(x_{0:t})=\mathbf1_{\{x_t=1\}}$, compute the asymptotic variance and verify the time-uniform bound.

items.title: Fixed-horizon asymptotic variance can grow without mixing
items.statement: Let $\mathsf X=\{0,1\}$ have the uniform target and proposal at time zero. Use identity mutation, unit incremental weights, and multinomial resampling at every time. For each fixed horizon $t$, take $\phi(x_{0:t})=\mathbf1_{\{x_t=1\}}$. Compute the fixed-horizon asymptotic variance and compare its dependence on $t$ with a time-uniform bound.
